title: Recursive binary search
summary: Recursively search ten sorted elements for 6, shrinking the search interval from [0, 9] to [0, 3] and then [2, 3], finally returning index 2.
context: The input consists of ten elements in increasing order at indices 0 through 9, with target 6; the full array is listed in the "Fixed sorted input" table. Here f(i, j) denotes searching the closed interval [i, j], with midpoint index m equal to floor((i + j) / 2).
description: After comparing the midpoint value against the target at each step, recursion enters only the single subinterval that could still contain the target. Excluded positions remain in the original array; once the target is hit, its index is returned directly without any merge step. The two tables below list the full input and the three calls.

frames.title: Recursive binary search
frames.explanation: The note at the bottom reads "The final result is index 2 for element 6". Counting by the closed intervals in the table, the number of candidates drops from 10 to 4 to 2, and the third call hits the target and returns immediately.

prose.title: Recursive binary search
prose.summary: Three states step through the three recursive calls in order, showing each call's current interval, midpoint, and next call or return value.
context: The target value is 6 and the input array never changes, so element values can be looked up in the "Fixed sorted input" table above; the parameters of all three calls can also be looked up by call in the "Three recursive calls" table.

steps.title: Inspect midpoint value 12
steps.explanation: On the initial closed interval [0, 9], compute midpoint m = floor((0 + 9) / 2) = 4, where the element at index 4 is 12. Since 12 > 6, the target can only lie in the left half; exclude indices 4 through 9 and recursively call f(0, 3).
steps.key_state: f(0, 9): midpoint m = 4 (value 12 > 6), recurse into left subinterval f(0, 3).
steps.announcement: Call f(0, 9); midpoint m = 4 has value 12, which is greater than target 6, so exclude indices 4 through 9 and recurse into f(0, 3).

steps.title: Inspect midpoint value 3
steps.explanation: On the closed interval [0, 3], compute midpoint m = floor((0 + 3) / 2) = 1, where the element at index 1 is 3. Since 3 < 6, the target can only lie in the right half; exclude indices 0 and 1 and recursively call f(2, 3).
steps.key_state: f(0, 3): midpoint m = 1 (value 3 < 6), recurse into right subinterval f(2, 3).
steps.announcement: Call f(0, 3); midpoint m = 1 has value 3, which is less than target 6, so exclude indices 0 and 1 and recurse into f(2, 3).

steps.title: Hit target value 6
steps.explanation: On the closed interval [2, 3], compute midpoint m = floor((2 + 3) / 2) = 2, where the element at index 2 is 6, matching the target value; return index 2 directly up the call chain with no combine step needed.
steps.key_state: f(2, 3): midpoint m = 2 (value 6 = 6), target found and index 2 returned.
steps.announcement: Call f(2, 3); midpoint index 2 has value 6, hitting the target and returning index 2 directly.
